name: Fortín T.
synopsis: Es la tranquila vida en un pueblo bonaerense de vanguardia
styleNotes:
1. Core Visual Philosophy: The Dollhouse Concept (Dockskåp)
Spatial Rigor: Compositions must be treated as rooms in a dollhouse. This involves a strict one-point linear perspective where the viewer looks into a space from a fixed, slightly elevated, or head-on position
.
The Frozen Moment (Frusna ögonblick): Avoid all dynamic movement or fluid action. Scenes should feel like a theatrical stage where the "curtain has just gone up," capturing a static instant suspended in time
.
Environmental Density: Every environment must be packed with meticulously detailed objects. In this project, this means 20th-century manual tools sitting alongside futuristic drone parts or holographic blueprints
.
2. Materiality and Medium
Base Technique: The visual foundation is watercolor and gouache applied to smooth cardboard (pannå). This creates a matte, analog texture with soft transitions
.
Graphite Underlay: Hard graphite textures from a number 4 pencil must be visible beneath the color. Use manual-style cross-hatching and shading for volume, which is then scanned or simulated digitally to maintain an organic, handcrafted feel
.
The "Lööf Line": Black contour lines are extremely thin, uniform, and sharp. Crucially, these lines are treated as the "final touch," added at the very end of the process to unify color blocks and define volumes
.
3. Architectural Logic: The "Skeva" Aesthetic
Geometric Deviation: Buildings and structures should have slight geometric imperfections known as "skeva" (crooked or skewed) walls. Avoid perfect digital right angles; structures should look realistic but manually constructed
.
Future Integration: Traditional Buenos Aires brick facades should be integrated with futuristic elements like sleek solar panels, glass domes, or mag-lev tracks, provided they are rendered with the same rigid, non-dynamic style [Turn 4, Turn 10].
Industrial Engineering Precision: Machinery, vehicles, and futuristic drones must be drawn with the precision of an industrial blueprint. This includes perfect concentric circles for wheels and visible rivets, even if the machine itself is a "fantasy product" that wouldn't work in reality
.
4. Character Design and Patterns
Rigid Anatomy: Characters should have a stiff, somewhat passive posture. Anatomical details include rounded heads and prominent, often spherical noses
.
Formal Attire: Clothing should remain classic formal (suits, long coats, caps). A signature Lööf trait is drawing patterns (like suit stripes) flat and orthogonal, completely ignoring the natural folds and shadows of the fabric
.
Flatness vs. Volume: While the environment uses perspective for depth, the textures on people and objects often remain intentionally flat, creating a unique visual tension
.
5. Technical Color Palette
The project utilizes a low-saturation, earthy palette to simulate Lööf’s mid-century "color phobia" era, using single points of high-intensity color to guide the eye
